Surah 114: Al-Nas (The Mankind)

Makki, though there is difference of opinion about it, and its verses are six.

﴿Say: I seek refuge﴾. It is also recited in both surahs (al-Falaq and al-Nas) with the hamzah omitted and its vowel transferred to the lam (i.e., "qul a'udhu" is read as "qul 'udhu" with the vowel of the hamzah placed on the preceding lam, giving "qul udhu" for the recitation).

﴿In the Lord of mankind﴾. That is: the Master of their affairs and the one who nurtures them, by bestowing what benefits them and warding off what harms them.

"And His saying: ﴿King of mankind﴾ is an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān), brought in to clarify that His nurturing of them, may He be exalted, is not in the manner of the nurturing of ordinary kings for those under their hands among their slaves; rather, it is in the manner of perfect dominion, comprehensive disposal, and overpowering authority."

Likewise His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the God of mankind﴾. This is to show that His dominion, may He be exalted, is not merely a matter of taking control over them, standing in charge of the management of their affairs and their governance, and taking responsibility for arranging the means of their protection and defense, which is the utmost that kings can do. Rather, it is by way of worship (ma'budiyyah), founded on divinity (uluhiyyah), which requires complete power over disposing of them in every respect: giving life and causing death, bringing into being and annihilating. The specification of the attribution to mankind, although all the worlds are included in the thread of His lordship (rububiyyah), sovereignty (malakutiyyah) and divinity (uluhiyyah), serves as guidance to the method of seeking refuge that is pleasing to Him, may He be exalted, and worthy of being granted protection. For the seeker of refuge's appeal to his Lord, and his affiliation to Him, may He be exalted, through being a lord-owned, owned and servant-of-God within a genus that is one of its individuals, is among the causes of greater mercy and compassion. His command, may He be exalted, to do so is among the indications of the generous promise of protection without doubt. And because that from whose evil one seeks refuge is Satan, who is known for his enmity toward them, the explicit mention of their inclusion in the thread of His worship and sovereignty, may He be exalted, alludes to their being saved from Satan's dominion and his authority over them, as His saying, may He be exalted, expresses: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾. Thus, whoever makes the basis for the specification of the attribution merely the fact that seeking refuge is from harms specific to human souls has fallen short in fulfilling the station's due. As for taking that from which refuge is sought in the preceding verses to be bodily harms, its status is known. And the repetition of the annexed noun (mudaf ilayh) is for greater disclosure, confirmation, and honoring through the attribution.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 114, verse 4:

﴿From the evil of the whisperer﴾ is a noun meaning "al-waswasah" (whispering), which is a faint sound, like "al-zilzal" (the earthquake) in the sense of "al-zalzalah" (the quaking). As for the verbal noun (masdar), it is "al-waswas" with a kasrah, and what is intended by it is the Shaytan, who is named by his action for the sake of emphasis, as if he were the very essence of whispering. ﴿Who withdraws﴾ is the one whose habit is to "khanasa" (withdraw, draw back), i.e., he draws back when the human being remembers his Lord.

﴿Who whispers into the breasts of mankind﴾ when they are heedless of His remembrance, exalted is He. The grammatical position (i'rab) of the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) is either the genitive, as a qualifier (wasf) of "the whisperer," or the nominative or accusative, as a dispraise (dhamm).

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 114, Verse 6:**

﴿From among the jinn and mankind.﴾ This clarifies "the one who whispers," indicating that it is of two kinds: jinn and human, as the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿the devils of mankind and the jinn﴾. Alternatively, it is related to "yuwaswisu" (whispers), meaning: it whispers into their breasts from the direction of the jinn and from the direction of mankind. It has also been permitted that it be a clarification of "an-nas" (mankind), on the basis that the term is also applied to the jinn, in accordance with the usage of *nafar* (group) and *rijal* (men) for them. However, this is not to be relied upon. Closer to this is that "an-nas" is intended to mean *an-nasi* (the forgetful), with the dropping of the *ya'* (final letter) occurring as it does in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿the day the caller calls﴾ (*yawma yad'u ad-da'i*). Then it is clarified by "the jinn and mankind," for every individual of the two groups is afflicted with forgetting the right of God, Exalted is He, except one whom the intercessions of His protection overtake and whom the vastness of His mercy encompasses. May God, Exalted is He, preserve us from heedlessness of His remembrance, and grant us success in fulfilling the due of His gratitude.

Completed by the praise and help of God is this noble *tafsir* (exegesis), and may God's blessings be upon our master Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions.

(p-218)
**Conclusion of the Author**

The humble servant, humbly beseeching his Lord, the Majestic, said: O God, O Guardian of protection and guidance, and Guide of those who have strayed to the paths of rectitude, Originator of creation, Owner of necks, upon You I rely, and to You is my return. You are the Helper of every bewildered and distressed one, and the Protector from every terrible and fearful thing. I take refuge in Your inviolable sanctuary from the calamities of the vicissitudes of time, and I seek shelter in Your secure protection, and I take refuge in Your mighty pillar. I ask You from the treasuries of Your hidden goodness, in the hidden recesses of Your secret, for the best of what the pen of creation has written, in matters of this world and the next. I seek refuge in You from the various kinds of trials and evils, especially feeling secure in the abode of delusion, and being deceived by its bliss and its splendor, and being seduced by its adornments and its finery. So protect me with Your protection, help me with Your care, and pour upon me from the radiant lights of the Divine and the flashing effects of the Holy, that which frees me from the dark obstacles and strips me of the bodily attachments. Refine my proud soul from the filth of natures and characters, and illuminate my hard heart with the glimmering rays of illumination, so that it may prepare to cross over the secrets of intimacy, and be readied for presence in the enclosures of holiness. Make me firm upon the paths of truth and guidance, and direct me to the ways of righteousness and piety. Make my most cherished aim the seeking of Your pleasure, and my most honored days the day of meeting You, the day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds, group by group. And gather me with those upon whom You have bestowed favor: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous, and how excellent these companions are.
